ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $AB$ intersects the coordinate axes at points $A(0, -3)$ and $B(-5, 0)$, respectively. Point $C$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$, and point $P$ is a point on the $y$-axis. Connecting $CP$, a perpendicular line to $CP$ is drawn from point $C$ intersecting segment $BO$ at point $Q$. Let $AP=m$ and $BQ=n$. Find the expression of $m$ as a function of $n$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let line $CE\perp OA$ at point E, and $CF\perp OB$ at point F,\\
then $E(0,-\frac{3}{2})$, $F(-\frac{5}{2},0)$, $\angle CEP=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$,\\
because $AP=m$, $BQ=n$,\\
thus $OQ=5-n$, $OP=3-m$,\\
therefore $QF=OQ-OF=5-n-\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}-n$, $PE=OE-OP=\frac{3}{2}-(3-m)=m-\frac{3}{2}$,\\
because $\angle CEP+\angle AOB=180^\circ$,\\
therefore $CE\parallel OB$,\\
therefore $\angle ECF=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle PCE+\angle PCF=90^\circ$,\\
because $\angle QCF+\angle PCF=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle PCE=\angle QCF$,\\
therefore $\triangle PCE\sim \triangle QCF$,\\
therefore $\frac{PE}{CE}=\frac{QF}{CF}$, i.e., $\frac{m-\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{5}{2}}=\frac{\frac{5}{2}-n}{\frac{3}{2}}$,\\
therefore $m=-\frac{5}{3}n+\frac{17}{3}$, hence the function expression of $m$ in terms of $n$ is $m=\boxed{-\frac{5}{3}n+\frac{17}{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the line $AB$ intersects the coordinate axes at points $A(0, -3)$ and $B(-5, 0)$, respectively. Point $C$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$, and point $P$ is a point on the $y$-axis. Connecting $CP$, a perpendicular line to $CP$ is drawn from point $C$ intersecting segment $BO$ at point $Q$. Let $AP=m$ and $BQ=n$. Find the expression of $m$ as a function of $n$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let line $CE\perp OA$ at point E, and $CF\perp OB$ at point F,\\
then $E(0,-\frac{3}{2})$, $F(-\frac{5}{2},0)$, $\angle CEP=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$,\\
because $AP=m$, $BQ=n$,\\
thus $OQ=5-n$, $OP=3-m$,\\
therefore $QF=OQ-OF=5-n-\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}-n$, $PE=OE-OP=\frac{3}{2}-(3-m)=m-\frac{3}{2}$,\\
because $\angle CEP+\angle AOB=180^\circ$,\\
therefore $CE\parallel OB$,\\
therefore $\angle ECF=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle PCE+\angle PCF=90^\circ$,\\
because $\angle QCF+\angle PCF=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle PCE=\angle QCF$,\\
therefore $\triangle PCE\sim \triangle QCF$,\\
therefore $\frac{PE}{CE}=\frac{QF}{CF}$, i.e., $\frac{m-\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{5}{2}}=\frac{\frac{5}{2}-n}{\frac{3}{2}}$,\\
therefore $m=-\frac{5}{3}n+\frac{17}{3}$, hence the function expression of $m$ in terms of $n$ is $m=\boxed{-\frac{5}{3}n+\frac{17}{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure there are two schematic diagrams, both drawing the coordinate axes, and the straight line AB intersects the negative y-axis at A and intersects the negative x-axis at B. Point C is located near the middle of line segment AB, and point P is on the y-axis; connect from C to P, and at the same time draw another line from C intersecting the segment BO on the x-axis at Q. In Figure 1, P is slightly below near O, and in Figure 2, P is above O, but the coordinate relationship is the same.
Reasoning: It is known that A=(0,-3), B=(-5,0), and C is the midpoint of AB, so C=((-5+0)/2,(0-3)/2)=(-5/2,-3/2). Because AP=m and P is on the y-axis, taking distance m upward from A according to the figure, P=(0,m-3). Because BQ=n and Q is on BO in the direction from B to O, Q=(-5+n,0). Thus vector CP=P-C=(5/2,m-3/2), vector CQ=Q-C=(n-5/2,3/2). According to the meaning of the problem, CQ is perpendicular to CP, so the dot product is 0: (5/2)(n-5/2)+(m-3/2)(3/2)=0. Simplifying gives 10n-25+6m-9=0, that is, 6m+10n=34, so 3m+5n=17. Therefore m=-(5/3)n+17/3.
